'''Derrick Williams''' (born May 25, 1991) is an [[United States|American]] college  basketball player with the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona Wildcats]]. He is considered one of the top prospects for the [[2011 NBA Draft]].<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Derrick-Williams-5811/ Draft Express]</ref>

==College career==
Derrick Williams originally committed to play at the University of Southern California but asked for a release from his letter of intent when head coach Tim Floyd resigned amid allegations of NCAA rules violations. <ref>[http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/sports_blog/2011/03/college-basketball-.html College basketball: Derrick Williams - the outlier who skirted the grassroots basketball hype machine and still made it - latimes.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> He was quickly recruited by first year Head Coach [[Sean Miller]] at the University of Arizona. 

===Freshman Year===
As a freshman Williams averaged 15.7 points per game and was named a freshman [[All-American]] and the [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10]] Freshman of the Year.<ref>[http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/033010aab.html Derrick Williams Named Freshman All-America]</ref><ref>[http://wildcat.arizona.edu/sports/derrick-williams-wins-pac-10-freshman-of-year-1.1259362 Derrick Williams wins Pac-10 Freshman of Year]</ref>  

Freshman year honors:
* Fred Enke Most Outstanding Player (Team co-MVP) 
* All PAC-10 team

===Sophomore Year===
Williams rose to national prominence in his sophomore year. He averaged 19.5 points and 8.3 rebounds per game. During the 2011 season, Williams led the NCAA in True Shooting percentage (.690) and Effective Field Goal percentage (.650), helping lead the Arizona Wildcats basketball team to a regular season PAC-10 championship. Williams was named the Pac-10 Player of the Year.<ref>[http://wildcat.arizona.edu/sports/williams-named-pac-10-player-of-the-year-1.2074189 Arizona Daily Wildcat - Williams named Pac-10 Player of the Year<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
Williams also contributed to the Wildcats' run in the NCAA men's basketball tournament. He made a critical block with less than 2 seconds against Memphis. <ref>[http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2011/mar/19/no-headline---2011-03-18-230954339423/ Tigers replay: Derrick Williams' block sealed Memphis' fate »<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  He had a 3 point play against the [[2010–11 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]], which advanced the Wildcats to the Sweet 16 of the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]].<ref>[http://arizona.sbnation.com/arizona-wildcats/2011/3/19/2059100/arizona-vs-texas-sweet-16-ncaa-tournament--wildcats-longhorns Arizona vs. Texas: Wildcats Advance, Defeating Longhorns 70-69 - SB Nation Arizona<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Williams then led Arizona to an upset victory over the #1-seeded [[2010–11 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] by a 16 point margin to advance into the Elite Eight, where they fell 65-63 to, future champion, [[2010-11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]].
